caption: How to use stump tiles
content: The stump tile @t{forest_gate.r} greatly expands the ways you can fill Areas. However, when it comes to meeting @g{rule/complete_block/stump}{the conditions for completing Areas}, the valid placements are more limited than they may seem.

content.caption: Example 1
content: Assuming your available tiles are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} @t{forest_open.1.dr} @t{forest_open.2s.r} @t{forest_open_road.r} @t{forest_gate.r} and their rotations, let's solve this Area.

First, focus on the cell @m{pending}. The tiles that can be placed here are @t{forest_road.2t.ur}, @t{forest_open.1.ur}, or one of the stump tiles @t{forest_gate.r} @t{forest_gate.d} @t{forest_gate.l} @t{forest_gate.u}. However, considering @g{tips/complete_block/common/candidate_2}{the possible tiles for the surrounding cells}, neither @t{forest_road.2t.ur} nor @t{forest_open.1.ur} can be placed, so we can see that we must place a stump tile.

Recall that stumps must form a facing pair with exactly one cell between them. For example, if you place the right-facing stump tile @t{forest_gate.r} here, the tile @t{forest_open.1.ul} two cells away blocks the space, making it impossible to form a pair.
As a result, the only tile that can be placed in the cell @m{pending} is the upward-facing stump tile @t{forest_gate.u}, and it follows that the pairing stump and the road are placed as follows.

Next, focus on the cell @m{pending}. The tiles that can be placed here are @t{forest_road.2t.dl}, @t{forest_open.1.dl}, or one of the stump tiles @t{forest_gate.r} @t{forest_gate.d} @t{forest_gate.l} @t{forest_gate.u}. However, among these, the only tile that can actually be placed is @t{forest_road.2t.dl}. For example, if you place the downward-facing stump tile @t{forest_gate.d}, you can place another stump two cells away, but you cannot run a road through the cell @m{unsatisfied} between the stumps.
By applying the same deduction to the remaining cells, the Area is completed as follows.

content.caption: Example 2
content: Assuming your available tiles are @t{forest_road.2s.lr} @t{forest_road.2t.dr} @t{forest_open.1.dr} @t{forest_open.2s.r} @t{forest_open_road.r} @t{forest_gate.r} and their rotations, let's solve this Area.

As with @g{tips/complete_block/open_road/where_to_place}{lots-with-road}, you can also @b{use the Note feature to narrow down where stumps can be placed}.
Start by marking every cell with @m{pending}, then remove the marks from cells where you determine that a stump tile cannot be placed.
First, stump tiles cannot be placed on the cells @m{unsatisfied} where roads enter the Area.
Also, if a stump tile were placed on the cell @m{info}, there would be no tile that could be placed on the neighboring cell @m{unsatisfied}.
For the same reason, stump tiles cannot be placed on any of the cells @m{unsatisfied}.
We can now see that if a stump tile were placed on the cell @m{info}, it could not form a pair in any direction, since none of the cells two spaces away are marked @m{pending}.
Continuing this process leaves the cells @m{pending} as the remaining candidates.
Since @b{stump tiles cannot be placed on cells without an @m{pending} mark}, we can use this information to make further deductions involving the other tiles.
Eventually, we can determine that the stump pair must be placed as shown below.
We'll skip the remaining steps, but continuing the logical deductions completes the Area as shown.
